summary: US and Iranian negotiators are exploring a gradual deal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz in exchange for sanctions relief, despite strong opposition from Gulf states. Meanwhile, Israel has deployed its sixth submarine, INS Drakon, as a direct message to Iran, and the UAE has suspended all Iranian flights and banking operations. The conflict remains highly active with ongoing missile tests, West Bank operations, and diplomatic friction.
key_points: US and Iranian negotiators in New York are exploring a gradual deal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz in exchange for US sanctions relief, though Gulf states oppose Iran using the strait as leverage. (Source: @naya_foriraq/91491)
The UAE has suspended all flights by Iranian airlines and restricted Bank Melli Iran branches in response to US sanctions, impacting economic and travel links. (Source: @mamlekate/104616)
Israel's sixth submarine, INS Drakon, arrived after a 23-day, 8,000 km voyage from Germany, serving as a strategic message to Iran. (Source: @manniefabian/59233)
The IDF seized weapons, including M16 rifles and sniper rifles, and uncovered tunnels up to 25 meters deep near Kalqilya in the West Bank. (Source: @yediotnews25/135314)
Iran conducted missile tests from several regions amidst the ongoing conflict and diplomatic negotiations. (Source: @naya_foriraq/91495)
Approximately six million barrels of Iranian crude oil, valued at $600 million, are transiting the Atlantic toward the United States. (Source: @VahidOnline/78511)
An Israeli soldier was seriously injured by a landmine explosion near the Binyamin checkpoint, highlighting persistent ground threats. (Source: @New_security8200/203914)
